conventions.convention: The fixed extremal RN background has m>0, q_e²+q_m²=m², domain ℝ_v × (0,∞)_r × S², signature (-,+,+,+), and metric g=-D dv²+2 dv dr+r²γ with D=(1-m/r)². The locus r=m is a local Killing horizon; no global event-horizon identification is asserted.

A reduced profile is a real C³ function ψ:ℝ×(0,∞)→ℝ, lifted independently of the sphere variable. The C³ wave operator is the metric trace of the C¹ Hessian. All radial derivatives hold v fixed in the regular ingoing chart.
Set φ=rψ and H=∂rφ(v,m). The charge is not ∂rψ alone. In the cited Aretakis Part I normalization H₀=∂rψ+ψ/m, this charge is H=mH₀.
Linear second-derivative growth is asserted only when H≠0 and φ(v,m)→0 as v→+∞. Horizon-trace decay is an additional hypothesis, not a consequence of charge conservation.

Coordinates v,r and background parameters have length units. The scalar unit is arbitrary, [φ]=[ψ] m, [H]=[ψ], and [φ_rr/v]=[ψ] m⁻². The scalar is neutral and does not source either fixed background field.
The geometric suppliers inherit Countable Choice for their tangent-bundle smooth structure; no stronger choice principle is invoked.

load_bearing.statement: Fix m>0 and real q_e,q_m with q_e²+q_m²=m². On ℝ_v×(0,∞)_r×S² use g=-D dv²+2 dv dr+r²γ, D=(1-m/r)². A reduced spherical scalar profile is real and C³; its spherical lift has wave operator given by the metric trace of its Hessian, equivalently the stated density formula. Set φ=rψ and take radial derivatives in the regular ingoing chart.

For any admissible neutral spherical C³ solution of □gψ=0 on the specified extremal RN background, φ=rψ has Hψ(v)=∂rφ(v,m) constant for every v∈ℝ. A nonzero charge gives a nonzero transverse derivative that does not tend to zero.

For an admissible neutral spherical C³ solution on the specified extremal RN background, if its constant charge H=∂rφ(v,m) is nonzero and φ(v,m)→0 as v→+∞, then ∂r²φ(v,m)/v→-H/m². This is conditional fixed-background growth, with no global decay, coupled perturbation, or nonlinear instability conclusion.

published_dependencies.used_for: The explicitly inherited Countable Choice assumption for the geometric suppliers.
The regular ingoing product domain, metric and Maxwell-field formulas, signature, units, and selected time orientation.
At M=m and Q²=m², r=m is a local null Killing horizon generated by ∂v, with the stated signed surface-gravity convention and κ=0.
Existence and uniqueness of the metric-compatible torsion-free connection, its Christoffel formula, and metric-compatible tensor differentiation.
The wave-operator density calculation. Its first-derivative coordinate proof supports the explicitly explained extension from smooth to C¹ vector fields; the actual gradient current is C².
Constancy of Hψ on the order-convex interval ℝ once its derivative vanishes.
Existence of the integral primitive of the continuous horizon trace and uniqueness of primitives up to a constant when integrating the exact horizon transport equation.
The tail estimate proving that the integral of a horizon trace tending to zero is o(v). The application uses a continuous primitive on [S,v] differentiable on (S,v).

seams_checked.note: This is a page-context prerequisite. The extremal scalar arguments do not invoke the subextremal photon-trapping conclusion or infer a wave estimate from it. The throat-scaling supplier retains its R>0 limit domain; the assigned items independently use the regular ingoing metric.

The actual item-level use is the wave-operator convention from def-emg-fx-wave-currents. The assigned definition explicitly extends the smooth-scalar operator to C³ scalars through the Hessian trace and justifies the density formula at the required regularity. No conditional energy or bootstrap estimate is strengthened into horizon decay.

This remains a page-context edge: the current emg-fx13 items do not cite the assigned charge or growth results as premises. Its test-field postulate distinguishes its charged complex scalar on the static exterior from a neutral scalar continued through the horizon, and does not import the conditional growth result or assert its decay hypothesis.
